rationale: The exact source product is managed OpenShift on IBM Cloud. Red Hat's official OpenShift page explicitly describes building/running AI and managing predictive and generative AI model lifecycles, providing a product-specific AI claim. The IBM managed-service page substantiates the named SKU and conventional provisioning/operations but does not establish inclusion of all general OpenShift AI lifecycle capabilities in that managed service or in the historical undated record. Best-supported binary is weak/forced AI-positive at OpenShift product-family level; not proof that IBM separately bundles OpenShift AI.
ai_type_rationale: OpenShift remains a meaningful general-purpose application/container platform for non-AI workloads; AI-model lifecycle is an additional capability, supporting AI-enabled.
version_scope: Record identifies Red Hat OpenShift managed on IBM Cloud, no version/date. Current Red Hat OpenShift feature evidence and IBM managed-service identity evidence coexist, but managed-SKU and historical AI-feature availability are unresolved.
issues: Labeler and blind disagreed on binary status.
Current general OpenShift AI capabilities may not be included in the source-record managed-service version/SKU.
